facts.statement: Four valid species of Paraisurus have been found in Europe, Asia, North America, and Australia.
facts.quote: It contains four valid species, which have been found in Europe, Asia, North America, and Australia.

facts.statement: The status of P. amudarjensis is debated, with some paleontologists considering it a possible synonym of P. compressus.
facts.quote: A fifth species, P. amudarjensis, is considered by some paleontologists a possible synonym of P. compressus, but is debated.

facts.statement: Paraisurus went extinct around the Albian-Cenomanian boundary, and a supposed Coniacian occurrence is likely a misidentified pseudoscapanorhynchid.
facts.quote: It went extinct around the Albian-Cenomanian boundary, as a supposed Coniacian occurrence of "P. sp." is likely a misidentified pseudoscapanorhynchid.

facts.statement: The parent group of Paraisurus is Paraisuridae.
Paraisurus belongs to the family Paraisuridae.
Paraisurus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Paraisurus lived from the Aptian to the Cenomanian, between 121.4 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Cenomanian (121.4 to 93.9 million years ago)
